questions.context:
A circuit consisting of a capacitor C, a resistor of resistance R and an ideal battery of emf V, as shown in figure is known as RC series circuit.
As soon as the circuit is completed by closing key \(\mathrm{S_1}\) (keeping \(\mathrm{S_2}\) open) charges begin to flow between the capacitor plates and the battery terminals. The charge on the capacitor increases and consequently the potential difference \(V_c\) (= q/C) across the capacitor also increases with time. When this potential difference equals the potential difference across the battery, the capacitor is fully charged (Q = VC). During this process of charging, the charge q on the capacitor changes with time t as
\(q = Q[1 - e^{-t/RC}]\)
The charging current can be obtained by differentiating it and using \(\frac{d}{dx}(e^{mx}) = m e^{mx}\).
Consider the case when R = 20 k\(\Omega\), C = 500 \(\mu\)F and V = 10 V.

questions._figure: REQUIRED - the passage says 'as shown in figure' and never states how the two keys sit in the circuit, which is what the sub-parts turn on. Read on MY OWN page: a rectangular loop carrying, on its upper arm, a capacitor labelled C; on its left arm, a resistor drawn as a zig-zag and labelled R; on its lower arm, a battery labelled V; and, in the middle of the loop, two switches drawn one above the other and labelled \(\mathrm{S_2}\) (upper) and \(\mathrm{S_1}\) (lower), each connecting the left branch to the right branch. Deliberately WITHHELD: which of the two branches each key completes, i.e. which one puts the battery in the loop and which one shorts it out - that is precisely the discrimination between sub-parts (i) and (ii). Page idx 18.
questions._flag: TAXONOMY GAP (minor) - this case study is an RC TRANSIENT (charging, decay, time constant). The live Physics axis has no such subtopic in any chapter, so all five siblings are filed on the closest fit, 'Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance' / 'Capacitors, Capacitance and their Combinations', which carries the Q = CV relation three of the four sub-parts rest on. A 'Charging and Discharging of a Capacitor (RC Circuit)' subtopic would be the name I would have wanted. The 55/1/1 opener reports the same gap independently on the same case study.

questions.stem:
(i) (1) What are coherent sources ? Why are they necessary for observing a sustained interference pattern ?
(2) Lights from two independent sources are not coherent. Explain.
(ii) Two slits 0.1 mm apart are arranged 1.20 m from a screen. Light of wavelength 600 nm from a distant source is incident on the slits.
(1) How far apart will adjacent bright interference fringes be on the screen ?
(2) Find the angular width (in degree) of the first bright fringe.
questions._flag: MARKING-SCHEME CONCESSION, recorded here rather than in `_cbseVoided` - under sub-part (ii)(2) the scheme prints 'Give full marks if the student writes the answer in radians only'. This is CONDITIONAL on the student's work being right (they must still reach the correct angular width, merely in radians rather than degrees), so by the addendum's rule table it is ordinary marking latitude and asserts nothing about the question. The question is NOT voided.

questions.stem:
(i) Define a wavefront. An incident plane wave falls on a convex lens and gets refracted through it. Draw a diagram to show the incident and refracted wavefront.
(ii) A beam of light coming from a distant source is refracted by a spherical glass ball (refractive index 1.5) of radius 15 cm. Draw the ray diagram and obtain the position of the final image formed.
questions._flag: CHAPTER NOTE - this question straddles two chapters. Sub-part (i) is Huygens' wavefront construction (Wave Optics); sub-part (ii) is successive refraction at two spherical surfaces of a glass sphere, which is Ray Optics and Optical Instruments / 'Refraction at Spherical Surfaces and by Lenses', and the marking scheme solves it that way. Filed on Wave Optics / Huygens Principle to keep it on the same chapter as the alternative it replaces, Q31(a), which is wholly Wave Optics.

questions.subtopic: Potential Energy of a System of Charges
questions.stem:
(i) Two point charges 5 \(\mu\)C and \(-1\) \(\mu\)C are placed at points \((-3\ \text{cm}, 0, 0)\) and \((3\ \text{cm}, 0, 0)\) respectively. An external electric field \(\vec{E} = \frac{A}{r^2}\hat{r}\) where \(A = 3 \times 10^5\) Vm is switched on in the region. Calculate the change in electrostatic energy of the system due to the electric field.
(ii) A system of two conductors is placed in air and they have net charge of \(+80\mu\)C and \(-80\mu\)C which causes a potential difference of 16 V between them.
(1) Find the capacitance of the system.
(2) If the air between the capacitor is replaced by a dielectric medium of dielectric constant 3, what will be the potential difference between the two conductors ?
(3) If the charges on two conductors are changed to \(+160\) \(\mu\)C and \(-160\) \(\mu\)C, will the capacitance of the system change ? Give reason for your answer.

(i) Consider three metal spherical shells A, B and C, each of radius R. Each shell is having a concentric metal ball of radius R/10. The spherical shells A, B and C are given charges \(+6q\), \(-4q\), and \(14q\) respectively. Their inner metal balls are also given charges \(-2q\), \(+8q\) and \(-10q\) respectively. Compare the magnitude of the electric fields due to shells A, B and C at a distance 3R from their centres.
(ii) A charge \(-6\) \(\mu\)C is placed at the centre B of a semicircle of radius 5 cm, as shown in the figure. An equal and opposite charge is placed at point D at a distance of 10 cm from B. A charge \(+5\) \(\mu\)C is moved from point 'C' to point 'A' along the circumference. Calculate the work done on the charge.
questions._figure: REQUIRED - sub-part (ii) says 'as shown in the figure' and the stem never says where C and A lie, which is the whole of the potential difference the work done depends on. Read on MY OWN page: a horizontal straight line carrying four labelled points, in the printed left-to-right order D, C, B, A, with a semicircular arc drawn above the line from C round to A; the charge \(+6q\) is marked at D and the charge \(-6q\) is marked at B. Deliberately WITHHELD: the spacings between the four points as drawn. Page idx 22.

The signs and positions agree; only the unit symbol differs. Not repaired in either direction.

questions.subtopic: Magnetic Force and Motion in a Magnetic Field
questions.stem:
(i) A proton moving with velocity \(\vec{V}\) in a non-uniform magnetic field traces a path as shown in the figure.
The path followed by the proton is always in the plane of the paper. What is the direction of the magnetic field in the region near points P, Q and R ? What can you say about relative magnitude of magnetic fields at these points ?
(ii) A current carrying circular loop of area A produces a magnetic field B at its centre. Show that the magnetic moment of the loop is \(\frac{2\mathrm{BA}}{\mu_0}\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{A}}{\pi}}\).
questions._figure: REQUIRED - sub-part (i) asks for the field direction and the relative field magnitudes at three points that exist only in the drawing. Read on MY OWN page: a shaded circle carrying a '+' sign, representing the proton, at the left, with a velocity vector \(\vec{V}\) labelled beside it; from it a path runs to the right, straight at first to a marked point P, then rising through a marked point Q to a marked point R near the top, and falling away to the right beyond R. Deliberately WITHHELD: the sense in which the path curves at each point and how tightly it is curved there - the first is what fixes the field's direction into or out of the page and the second is what fixes the ordering of the field magnitudes, i.e. both of the things the question asks for. Page idx 22.

questions.subtopic: Torque on a Current Loop and Magnetic Dipole
questions.stem:
(i) Derive an expression for the torque acting on a rectangular current loop suspended in a uniform magnetic field.
(ii) A charged particle is moving in a circular path with velocity \(\vec{V}\) in a uniform magnetic field \(\vec{B}\). It is made to pass through a sheet of lead and as a consequence, it looses one half of its kinetic energy without change in its direction. How will (1) the radius of its path (2) its time period of revolution change ?
questions._flag: TRANSCRIBED AS PRINTED - sub-part (ii) reads 'it looses one half of its kinetic energy' where it means 'loses'. Not repaired; the stem is faithful to page idx 22.
